svg.title: Layered explanation of eventual consistency
svg.desc: Four stacked layers of increasing depth. Gist: copies agree eventually if updates stop. Model: replicas accept writes and propagate them asynchronously, so reads may be stale. Practitioner: trade-offs between consistency, availability and latency, conflict resolution and quorums. Expert: formal consistency models and open research problems. An arrow notes that each layer should be tested unaided before moving up.
svg.text: One concept, four layers of explanation
Formal consistency models compared; proofs of
Trade-offs between consistency, availability and latency; conflict
resolution rules; quorum reads and writes; how stale reads show up
Each replica accepts writes and passes them on later, so a read
may reach a replica that has not yet received the latest update
Copies of the data may briefly disagree, but they all agree once updates stop arriving.
Move up only after explaining the layer below unaided; stop at the layer the goal requires.
Example: eventual consistency in replicated databases.
